title: Jerome "Chef" McElroy

Final: Jerome "Chef" McElroywas a beloved fixture inSouth Park, serving as the soulful cook atSouth Park Elementaryand the kids' unofficial life coach. Known for his smooth voice and tendency to burst into seductive ballads about love (and usually sex), Chef became a go-to source of wisdom forthe boys—even if his advice occasionally veered wildly off-topic. He made his debut in the very first episode, "Cartman Gets an Anal Probe," and was voiced byIsaac Hayes.

Chef met his bizarre and untimely end in theSeason Tenpremiere, "The Return of Chef," after allegedly joining the mysterious "Super Adventure Club", a group with questionable hobbies and a suspiciously catchy theme song. His departure from the show followed real-life tensions with Hayes, who left the series after it aired "Trapped in the Closet"—a satirical episode skewering Scientology. Rumors persist that the episode was actually written by a team of rogue dolphins, though this has never been confirmed.

Background: As his nickname implies, Chef was aschool cafeteriacook at the South Park Elementary School and former member ofCity Councilas "Head of Public Safety". He was the only adult that the boys (Stan,Kyle,Cartman, andKenny) consistently looked to for advice. A typical exchange between Chef and the boys goes as such:

Chef used the word "children" often, even for a singular child. For example, he referred to Cartman as "children" in "Cartman's Mom is a Dirty S***" and "Spontaneous Combustion", Stan in "Kenny Dies", andButtersin "The Simpsons Already Did It". He also tended to use "fudge" as a euphemism for "f***", particularly in early episodes. The various humorously named snacks he made in "Chef's Chocolate Salty Balls" epitomized this.

While most of the inhabitants of South Park are Caucasian, Chef was one of the very few residents in town who was African American; in fact, the only other black people to consistently live in South Park areTolkienand his parents, who were not prominent characters until the fourth season. As a result, Chef (usually affectionately, though not always) referred to most people in town with the racial slur "cracker", often "cracker-ass", including the children.

Aside from cooking, Chef was passionate about singing - he wrote the song, "Stinky Britches" which was later covered byAlanis Morissette. Chef was based on such 1970s African American singers as Isaac Hayes and Barry White. Typically, he agreed to give the boys advice in the form of songs but wound up singing about having sex. However, over time, like many earlier characters on the show, his role, especially as a singer, diminished, and in later seasons, Chef did not sing much. By the time his death occurred, Chef had not sung any songs in four years or so, with one of the last examples of him singing being "The Simpsons Already Did It".

Despite his preoccupations with women and sex, Chef was generally one of the few level-headed adults in South Park. In addition to dispensing advice to "the children", Chef spoke out against outrageous ideas and helped save South Park/the world in general from disasters on numerous occasions. However, Chef was not above performing nonsensical acts, such asbuying a fancy TV that he could not even program.
Chef would often explain mature themes tothe boys.

In earlier seasons, Chef was often approached by the children when they were unfamiliar with a sexual term or practice. This happened so often that it eventually got on Chef's nerves, leading him to say, "Goddammit, children, why do I always have to be the one to teach you these things?", but went on to explain to them whatever they wanted to know anyway.
Chef's last name suggests he could be at least partially of some Celtic descent, and indeed his parents live in Edinburgh, Scotland.
In "Chef Goes Nanners", he briefly converted to Islam and adopted the name "Abdul Mohammed Jabar Rauf Kareem Ali", but converted back to Christianity by the end of the episode.

In "Chef Aid", the boys attempt to help Chef out of jail by organizing a "Chef Aid" concert featuring many celebrities who Chef was friends with. Death: The fate of Chef was sealed in the Season 10 premiere, in which voice clips taken from previous episodes were linked together to form new dialogue to support the plot of "The Return of Chef". In the episode, Chef was brainwashed into becoming a child molester by the Super Adventure Club, an organization which combines outdoors activities with sex tourism and bizarre religious beliefs, some of which seem akin to those held by the real-life Church of Scientology. Chef was killed off because the voice actor was a Scientologist, and left the show because of it's mockery of Scientology.

At the end of the episode Chef dies a very unnecessarily violent and painful death. He tries to leave the club and go back to South Park with the boys, but then gets convinced to go back to the club byConellywho tells him "Don't you remember why you left South Park?". Chef walks back through the bridge, apologizing to the kids, and telling them to get out of his mind. Then he gets struck with a lighting bolt, which causes the bridge to break, making him fall, and also burning him alive. While falling he hits a few rocks before finally getting impaled on a branch. Then a mountain lion appears, trying to rip chef's arm off, while the club members try shooting at it, and miss and accidentally hit Chef repeatedly instead. Then a grizzly bear appears and tries to kill the lion to have chef all to itself. The lion pounces on the bear, and the bear throws the lion off. The 2 decide to share Chef's corpse, and the bear takes Chef's leg, while the lion rips off chef's face, and takes his arm.Kyle, utterly horrified at the death, angrily yells at the club members for letting Chef die like that. ThenCartmangives the boys a last ray of hope, saying "Maybe- maybe he's still okay. No really- they say the last thing you do before you die is crap your pa-" Then Chef's already battered corpse violently shits its pants before dying. Confirming his death.

The town held a moving memorial service for him, in which Kyle gave a eulogy stating, "We shouldn't be mad at Chef for leaving us; we should be mad at that fruity little club for scrambling his brains" - a not-so-subtle jab at Scientology.

Chef's body was secretly recovered by the Super Adventure Club, who managed to revive him as a "Darth" Chef, mimicking the ending toStar Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith. He was revived by the Super Adventure Club in a Darth Vader-esque suit (albeit with a helmet similar to a chef's hat) and was given a red spatula lightsaber. After that, the Super Adventure Club leaderConnellybegan the scene, which parodiesRevenge of the Sith:

Darth Chef's voice was provided byPeter Serafinowicz, who voiced Darth Maul inStar Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace. However, he has not reappeared. It should be noted the name "Darth Chef" has been generally accepted by fans, but is never actually used on the show. It is, however, mentioned onSouth Park Studios.

Isaac Hayes QuitsSouth Park: On March 13, 2006, Isaac Hayes quitSouth Park, reportedly over objections to the show's attitudes toward and depiction of various religions, claiming that the show had crossed the line from satire into intolerance.

However, despite the content of the official press release, there remained considerable speculation about the motivations behind his departure.Trey ParkerandMatt Stoneassumed that he quit due to the controversial episode "Trapped in the Closet", and its treatment of Scientology, as Hayes was a member of the religion. Series co-creator and writer Stone commented in a manner that suggested that Hayes practiced a double standard regarding the treatment of religion onSouth Park: "[We] never heard a peep out of Isaac in any way until we did Scientology. He wants a different standard for religions other than his own, and to me, that is where intolerance and bigotry begin."

Others suggested that Hayes left the show because of the external pressure forced by his fellow Scientologists and that the decision was not voluntary. It was eventually reported, however, that he did not quit the show, but that the original press release announcing his departure was put out by someone who was not authorized to represent him. On January 4, 2006, he defendedSouth Park'sstyle of controversial humor toThe Onion's AV Club and XM's Opie and Anthony Show, going so far as to note that although he was not pleased with the show's depiction of Scientology, he "understand[s] what [Matt and Trey] are doing."

It was later revealed by his son, Isaac Hayes III, that Hayes had suffered a severe stroke that left him unable to speak or make decisions on his own. The decision to quitSouth Parkand the statement were made by members of his entourage who were fellow Scientologists, and not by Hayes himself. Regardless of who made the press release, Hayes was in no condition to keep voicing Chef.
He died of a stroke on August 10, 2008, making "The Return of Chef" Chef's final official appearance in the show.

He was also often seen wearing a white apron with the word "Chef" printed on it. He appeared to be slightly overweight and had a black beard. In "Cartman Gets an Anal Probe" his apron text changes from an uppercase "CHEF" to a lowercase "chef" in one scene.

Even when he is employed as an accountant in "The Succubus", his signature hat can be seen hanging up in his office. However, he does not wear it as a young adult in the flashbacks in "Chef Aid" or "Cartman's Mom is a Dirty S***".

When the player takes Chef's health down to 1 (from a rather large 73,476 if you are level 15), he will fully regain control of himself and proclaim "Children! Everybody! I'm back!" before Clyde will throw a Molotov Cocktail at him, causing him to violently burst into flames and run around. The player will charge up and release a powerful fart, to which Chef gets caught in the proceeding fireball, killing him and causing him to re-sustain the brutal injuries that led to his original death, albeit him now being horribly charred. If the player fails to do this quickly, then he will set the player and their buddy on fire unless they have any shields. Once they have no shields, then they will get fire damage and will die soon meaning that they will have to restart the game from the last checkpoint.
Aside from his boss fight, Chef's picture is also seen on the "Hall of Honor" along with deceased faculty members and students.

Jerome "Chef" McElroywas a beloved fixture inSouth Park, serving as the soulful cook atSouth Park Elementaryand the kids' unofficial life coach. Known for his smooth voice and tendency to burst into seductive ballads about love (and usually sex), Chef became a go-to source of wisdom forthe boys—even if his advice occasionally veered wildly off-topic. ## Background
As his nickname implies, Chef was aschool cafeteriacook at the South Park Elementary School and former member ofCity Councilas "Head of Public Safety". He was the only adult that the boys (Stan,Kyle,Cartman, andKenny) consistently looked to for advice. A typical exchange between Chef and the boys goes as such:

Chef used the word "children" often, even for a singular child. For example, he referred to Cartman as "children" in "Cartman's Mom is a Dirty S***" and "Spontaneous Combustion", Stan in "Kenny Dies", andButtersin "The Simpsons Already Did It". He also tended to use "fudge" as a euphemism for "f***", particularly in early episodes. The various humorously named snacks he made in "Chef's Chocolate Salty Balls" epitomized this.

While most of the inhabitants of South Park are Caucasian, Chef was one of the very few residents in town who was African American; in fact, the only other black people to consistently live in South Park areTolkienand his parents, who were not prominent characters until the fourth season. As a result, Chef (usually affectionately, though not always) referred to most people in town with the racial slur "cracker", often "cracker-ass", including the children.

Aside from cooking, Chef was passionate about singing - he wrote the song, "Stinky Britches" which was later covered byAlanis Morissette. Chef was based on such 1970s African American singers as Isaac Hayes and Barry White. Typically, he agreed to give the boys advice in the form of songs but wound up singing about having sex. However, over time, like many earlier characters on the show, his role, especially as a singer, diminished, and in later seasons, Chef did not sing much. By the time his death occurred, Chef had not sung any songs in four years or so, with one of the last examples of him singing being "The Simpsons Already Did It".

Despite his preoccupations with women and sex, Chef was generally one of the few level-headed adults in South Park. In addition to dispensing advice to "the children", Chef spoke out against outrageous ideas and helped save South Park/the world in general from disasters on numerous occasions. However, Chef was not above performing nonsensical acts, such asbuying a fancy TV that he could not even program.

Chef would often explain mature themes tothe boys.

In earlier seasons, Chef was often approached by the children when they were unfamiliar with a sexual term or practice. This happened so often that it eventually got on Chef's nerves, leading him to say, "Goddammit, children, why do I always have to be the one to teach you these things?", but went on to explain to them whatever they wanted to know anyway.

Chef's last name suggests he could be at least partially of some Celtic descent, and indeed his parents live in Edinburgh, Scotland.

In "Chef Goes Nanners", he briefly converted to Islam and adopted the name "Abdul Mohammed Jabar Rauf Kareem Ali", but converted back to Christianity by the end of the episode.

## Death
Chef's gruesome corpse.

The fate of Chef was sealed in the Season 10 premiere, in which voice clips taken from previous episodes were linked together to form new dialogue to support the plot of "The Return of Chef". In the episode, Chef was brainwashed into becoming a child molester by the Super Adventure Club, an organization which combines outdoors activities with sex tourism and bizarre religious beliefs, some of which seem akin to those held by the real-life Church of Scientology. Chef was killed off because the voice actor was a Scientologist, and left the show because of it's mockery of Scientology.

At the end of the episode Chef dies a very unnecessarily violent and painful death. He tries to leave the club and go back to South Park with the boys, but then gets convinced to go back to the club byConellywho tells him "Don't you remember why you left South Park?". Chef walks back through the bridge, apologizing to the kids, and telling them to get out of his mind. Then he gets struck with a lighting bolt, which causes the bridge to break, making him fall, and also burning him alive. While falling he hits a few rocks before finally getting impaled on a branch. Then a mountain lion appears, trying to rip chef's arm off, while the club members try shooting at it, and miss and accidentally hit Chef repeatedly instead. Then a grizzly bear appears and tries to kill the lion to have chef all to itself. The lion pounces on the bear, and the bear throws the lion off. The 2 decide to share Chef's corpse, and the bear takes Chef's leg, while the lion rips off chef's face, and takes his arm.Kyle, utterly horrified at the death, angrily yells at the club members for letting Chef die like that. ThenCartmangives the boys a last ray of hope, saying "Maybe- maybe he's still okay. No really- they say the last thing you do before you die is crap your pa-" Then Chef's already battered corpse violently shits its pants before dying. Confirming his death.

The town held a moving memorial service for him, in which Kyle gave a eulogy stating, "We shouldn't be mad at Chef for leaving us; we should be mad at that fruity little club for scrambling his brains" - a not-so-subtle jab at Scientology.

## Isaac Hayes QuitsSouth Park
Isaac Hayesvoiced Chef from 1997 to 2006.

On March 13, 2006, Isaac Hayes quitSouth Park, reportedly over objections to the show's attitudes toward and depiction of various religions, claiming that the show had crossed the line from satire into intolerance.

However, despite the content of the official press release, there remained considerable speculation about the motivations behind his departure.Trey ParkerandMatt Stoneassumed that he quit due to the controversial episode "Trapped in the Closet", and its treatment of Scientology, as Hayes was a member of the religion. Series co-creator and writer Stone commented in a manner that suggested that Hayes practiced a double standard regarding the treatment of religion onSouth Park: "[We] never heard a peep out of Isaac in any way until we did Scientology. He wants a different standard for religions other than his own, and to me, that is where intolerance and bigotry begin."

Others suggested that Hayes left the show because of the external pressure forced by his fellow Scientologists and that the decision was not voluntary. It was eventually reported, however, that he did not quit the show, but that the original press release announcing his departure was put out by someone who was not authorized to represent him. On January 4, 2006, he defendedSouth Park'sstyle of controversial humor toThe Onion's AV Club and XM's Opie and Anthony Show, going so far as to note that although he was not pleased with the show's depiction of Scientology, he "understand[s] what [Matt and Trey] are doing."

It was later revealed by his son, Isaac Hayes III, that Hayes had suffered a severe stroke that left him unable to speak or make decisions on his own. The decision to quitSouth Parkand the statement were made by members of his entourage who were fellow Scientologists, and not by Hayes himself. Regardless of who made the press release, Hayes was in no condition to keep voicing Chef.

He died of a stroke on August 10, 2008, making "The Return of Chef" Chef's final official appearance in the show.
